title: Strawberry-Vanilla Pancakes
changes_from_base: The same buttermilk and soured cream batter, but each pancake is scattered with chopped strawberries tossed in vanilla and sugar before it is flipped.
summary: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes studded with sweetened fresh strawberries and a hint of vanilla, perfect for a lazy weekend breakfast.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: caster sugar (2 tbsp for the batter, 1 tbsp for the strawberries)
fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 93°C, spray the wire rack with oil and set it on its tray ready to hold the cooked pancakes.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 283 g plain flour with 2 tbsp caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In another bowl whisk 480 ml buttermilk, 2 eggs, 60 ml soured cream and 42 g melted butter, pour this into a well in the flour mix and stir gently until just combined and lumpy, then rest the batter 10 min.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Toss the 283 g chopped strawberries with ½ tsp vanilla and 1 tbsp caster sugar.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a 30 cm non-stick pan over medium heat, wipe out with kitchen paper to leave a thin film, then cook 4 pancakes of 60 ml batter each until the edges set, the base turns golden and bubbles start to break, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Sprinkle 1 tbsp of the strawberry mixture over each pancake, flip and cook until golden, a further 1-2 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Serve straight away or keep warm on the rack in the oven, repeating with the rest of the batter and adding more oil as needed.

tips: Toss the chopped strawberries with the vanilla and sugar a few minutes ahead so they turn juicy, then scatter them over each pancake just before you flip it.
Don't overmix the batter - a few lumps and streaks of flour keep the pancakes tender.
Wipe excess oil from the pan before each batch so the pancakes brown rather than fry.
Keep finished pancakes on a warm rack in a low oven so the whole batch can be served together.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
